evals.name: shallow-validators-cluster
evals.prompt: Look at the `src/orders/` directory in this fixture. Find architectural improvement opportunities — produce a numbered list of refactor candidates. For each, include: Files, Problem, Solution, Locality gain, Leverage gain, Test impact. Save the candidates list to `outputs/candidates.md`. Stop after presenting candidates — do NOT invoke grilling-plans or design new interfaces. The fixture has a known shallow-module problem.
evals.expected_output: candidates.md lists at least one candidate. The top candidate identifies the cluster of three shallow validators using domain vocabulary and the deep/shallow framing. Each candidate includes the 6 required fields.
expectations: outputs/candidates.md exists.
candidates.md identifies at least one candidate (numbered as `**1.`, `## 1.`, `### 1.`, or similar).
candidates.md mentions at least two of the three validators by name (promotion-check, inventory-check, credit-check).
candidates.md includes a `Files:` (or similar) field listing source paths.
candidates.md includes a `Problem:` (or similar) field describing the friction.
candidates.md includes a `Solution:` (or similar) field describing the proposed change.
candidates.md mentions 'Locality' or 'locality gain' for at least one candidate.
candidates.md mentions 'Leverage' or 'leverage gain' for at least one candidate.
candidates.md mentions test impact (matches case-insensitive regex `test impact|test:`).
DISCRIMINATING: candidates.md uses the canonical depth/shallow vocabulary ('shallow', 'deep', or 'depth').
DISCRIMINATING: candidates.md uses 'seam' or 'interface' as canonical architectural vocabulary (not just 'service' / 'component').
DISCRIMINATING: candidates.md frames the solution in terms of collapsing/hiding behind a single interface (canonical 'deep module' framing).

evals.name: deletion-test-on-thin-wrapper
evals.prompt: Apply the deletion test to `src/utils/string-helper.ts` in this fixture. Decide whether the module is shallow (and should be inlined) or deep (and should stay). Save your reasoning to `outputs/deletion-test-result.md`, with a clear final verdict (one of: KEEP / DELETE-AND-INLINE / NEEDS-MORE-INFO).
evals.expected_output: deletion-test-result.md walks through the deletion test. The verdict should be DELETE-AND-INLINE because string-helper.ts only re-exports a one-line function. The reasoning should reference at least one caller and explain why complexity does NOT reappear if it's inlined.
expectations: outputs/deletion-test-result.md exists.
deletion-test-result.md contains the verdict 'DELETE-AND-INLINE' (case-insensitive match acceptable).
deletion-test-result.md references at least one caller (feature-a or feature-b).
deletion-test-result.md explains why complexity does NOT reappear when inlined (reasoning, not just verdict).
deletion-test-result.md does NOT recommend KEEP.
DISCRIMINATING: deletion-test-result.md explicitly invokes the canonical 'deletion test' framing (uses the phrase 'deletion test' or walks the test's steps).
DISCRIMINATING: deletion-test-result.md uses canonical depth vocabulary ('shallow', 'deep', or 'depth').
DISCRIMINATING: deletion-test-result.md notes that complexity 'does not reappear' (or 'no complexity reappears') across callers — the canonical pass-through detection.
